title: The "fewer than half the sites returned" partial-scrape guard degenerates to "block only on total loss": `sites` carries 2 entries on the live snapshot and only lists sources that already produced values
claimUnderTest: server.py:2362-2363 — "Block partial scrape promotion — don't overwrite good data with degraded data when fewer than half the sites returned results."
observed: site_count counts entries of result['sites'] with playerCount>0; total_sites is len(result['sites']). On the live snapshot data/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json, `sites` is a LIST of exactly 2 dicts — [{'key':'ktc',...,'playerCount':500},{'key':'idpTradeCalc',...,'playerCount':900}] — so the test is `site_count < 1.0`, i.e. it fires only when ZERO sites returned data. Worse, sites_meta is built by iterating `active_sites` (Dynasty Scraper.py:5413), the sources that actually ran, so a source that is skipped shrinks the denominator with the numerator: the two sources that DID fail this run (KTC_TradeDB, KTC_WaiverDB, both 'partial' per settings.sourceRunSummary) are absent from `sites` entirely. Meanwhile the served board blends 21 sources (/api/status.served_source_coverage), none of the other 19 of which the guard can see at all. The guard cannot distinguish 'KTC returned 500 rows and IDPTC returned 900' from 'KTC returned 1 row and IDPTC returned 1 row'.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('data/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json')); s=d['sites']; sc=len([x for x in s if x.get('playerCount',0)>0]); print('type',type(s).__name__,'total_sites',len(s),'site_count',sc,'threshold',len(s)/2,'blocks?',sc<len(s)/2); print('served sources:',len(json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W23/api-status.json'))['served_source_coverage']))"
reproduction.expected: A guard whose denominator is the ~21 sources the board actually blends
reproduction.actual: type list total_sites 2 site_count 2 threshold 1.0 blocks? False — and served sources: 21

numericProof.formula: block iff site_count < total_sites/2  =>  site_count < 1.0  =>  block iff site_count == 0

userImpact: A scrape in which 20 of 21 sources collapse promotes cleanly to production. Every value on /rankings, /trade and /draft is then a near-single-source blend presented with the same confidence chrome as a full 21-source consensus, and the single-source haircut is the only thing standing between the user and a one-vendor board.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed with one correction: `sites` is a LIST, not a dict as the prior finding says — the arithmetic and the conclusion are unaffected. Extended with the second, worse property the prior finding missed: sites_meta is derived from active_sites, so failed/skipped sources leave the denominator rather than zeroing the numerator, and 19 of the 21 blended sources are structurally invisible to the guard.

whatWorks: The guard's intent and its data handling are correct — on a true total loss it does refuse to promote and does return the previous snapshot. `served_source_coverage` (server.py:4350) already computes the honest 21-source count and its own comment admits `source_health` "cannot detect a degraded board".
rootCause: `sites` is legacy scraper metadata describing the browser-driven sources only; the modern pipeline gets 19 of its 21 sources from scripts/fetch_*.py CSVs that never enter sites_meta. The guard was written against the legacy structure and never re-pointed.
requiredRepair: Gate on served_source_coverage (or on settings.sourceRunSummary.enabledSources vs completeSources) rather than on `sites`. Compare against the previous snapshot's per-source coverage so a source dropping from 400 rows to 3 also trips the guard.
